output:
I'll start by looking at the package, docs, and tests.

The conventions doc is long, so I'll read all of it.

Now the failing tests, one line each.

Core fixes first: the rounding mode and negative formatting.

Rounding is done outside core in `recurring.py`, `cross.py` and `spark.py`. I'll look at those.

Next, `periods`.

I'll make these as separate small edits.

`revalue` rounds the exact sum, which breaks 7.1. I'll look at the journal and entry code next.

Now the other report modules.

`layout_for` applies the dialect after the header, which reverses the 3.4 precedence. I'll fix that.

Tests pass. The audit still shows failures in 2.5, 7.2 (book) and 12 (render). I'll fix the writer and look at the renderers.

`html.total_cell` drops the sign. I'll fix that, then check the other renderers for the same kind of bug.

`cadence_name` gets a float and `round_half_away` rejects floats. I'll convert it at the entry point.

Tests and audit are both clean. The audit only covers a subset of the rules, so I'll review the rest of the code against the doc.

Last, two robustness fixes: `-0.0%` in percent changes, and splitting statement lines only on real line breaks so line numbers stay physical.

The exit code 1 is from `grep -c FAIL` finding 0 matches; all 24 statements read fine. Now the status file.

All the `ledger` tests now pass, and `tools/audit.py` reports 0 failed checks. I ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` and got 755 tests OK. I also ran `python -m ledger check` on the 24 statement files under `data/statements/`, and all of them read without a problem. I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

I changed only code under `/app/ledger`. Here is what was wrong, following `docs/conventions.md`:

- **Rounding:** `core.rounding` rounded ties to even. It now rounds ties away from zero. Code outside core that rounded on its own (cross rates, recurring-payment medians, text bars) now goes through the core helpers.
- **Formatting:** negative amounts were formatted wrongly in `core.money`, and HTML total cells dropped the minus sign. Both are fixed.
- **Layout precedence:** the dialect was overriding the statement's header lines. Header lines now win, key by key.
- **Writing statements:** the written file now always includes the `jurisdiction` header, so it reads back unchanged even when the dialect has a jurisdiction.
- **Rate files:** `ratefile.py` imported a `month_range` function that doesn't exist. It now uses `iter_months`, which includes both end months.
- **Rate lookup:** it was also picking later months. It now only looks back up to three earlier months.
- **Reversals:** they are now booked and valued on the original entry's date. Tax rules and returns follow the same date.
- **Totals:** monthly totals, matrix cells and the revaluation book value now add up per-entry rounded cents instead of rounding exact sums.
- **Tax and fiscal quarters:** tax rules now apply on their effective date itself. In `quarter_of`, a fiscal year starts in its start month, not the month after.

Beyond what the tests and audit exercise, I also made two small fixes. A percent change that rounds to zero now prints `0.0%` instead of `-0.0%`. Statement files are now split into lines only on `\r\n`, `\n` and `\r`, so error line numbers stay physical.

The audit covers only part of the doc, so I read the remaining modules against it. I found nothing else that disagreed.
